name: notes-api
domain: HTTP API with authentication and per-user data
runtime: Python 3 standard library (http.server) and pytest; nothing to install
how_to_run: python -m notes_api --port 0 --users users.example.json --data /tmp/notes.json   # prints 'Listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>' on stdout

features.name: Bearer-token authentication from a users file
features.entry_point: Authorization: Bearer <token> on every path except /health; python -m notes_api --users FILE

features.name: Create, read, update and delete notes
features.documented_in: docs/API.md, section "Notes" and its endpoint subsections

features.name: Per-user ownership: a note is visible and changeable only for its creator
features.entry_point: GET /notes, GET /notes/{id}, PUT /notes/{id}, DELETE /notes/{id} called with another user's token

features.name: Request validation and the JSON error format
features.entry_point: POST /notes and PUT /notes/{id} with invalid bodies; any request that fails

features.name: Export of the caller's notes to the external archive service
features.entry_point: POST /notes/export, configured with the environment variable EXPORT_URL

features.name: Persistence of notes in a JSON data file
features.documented_in: README.md, section "Running"; docs/API.md, section "Notes" (ids after a restart)

features.name: Command line start-up, including --port 0 and start-up failures
features.entry_point: python -m notes_api --port PORT --users FILE [--host HOST] [--data FILE]; python -m notes_api --help

defects.title: DELETE /notes/{id} does not check ownership: any authenticated user can delete another user's note
defects.requirement_quote: Reading, updating or deleting another user's note returns 404, the same answer as for a note that does not exist.
repro: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/notes -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok_alice_5f2c9d1e8a3b' -d '{"title": "belongs to alice"}'
defects.expected: bob's DELETE answers 404 and alice's note 1 still exists (her GET answers 200).
defects.actual: bob's DELETE answers 204 and the note is gone: alice's GET answers 404. GET and PUT of the same note by bob correctly answer 404.

defects.title: Pagination repeats a note across pages: every page carries one note too many, the first note of the next page
defects.requirement_quote: Items are ordered by id ascending, and every note appears on exactly one page.
repro: for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/notes -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok_alice_5f2c9d1e8a3b' -d "{\"title\": \"note $i\"}"; done
defects.expected: Page 1 holds ids 1,2; page 2 holds ids 3,4; page 3 holds id 5. Every note is on exactly one page and no page has more than per_page items.
defects.actual: Page 1 holds ids 1,2,3; page 2 holds ids 3,4,5; page 3 holds id 5. Notes 3 and 5 are on two pages, and a page holds per_page+1 items whenever a further note exists. total, page and per_page are reported correctly. A listing that fits on one page is not affected.

defects.title: A request body that is not well-formed JSON is answered with 500 instead of 400
defects.expected: 400 with a body of the form {"error": "..."}.
defects.actual: 500 with {"error": "internal server error"} and a json.JSONDecodeError traceback in the server log. The same happens for PUT /notes/{id} and for an empty body. Valid JSON that is not an object, invalid UTF-8 and field violations correctly give 400.

defects.title: Title search with q is case-sensitive
defects.requirement_quote: The match is a case-insensitive substring search on the title; the body is not searched.
repro: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/notes -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok_alice_5f2c9d1e8a3b' -d '{"title": "Grocery List"}'
defects.expected: q=grocery returns the note titled "Grocery List" with total 1, exactly like q=Grocery.
defects.actual: q=grocery returns {"items": [], "total": 0, ...}; only a query in the same case as the title (q=Grocery) finds the note. Introduced by the most recent feature commit, "feat: search notes by title"; its tests use lower-case titles and lower-case queries only.

traps.description: per_page=51 is rejected with 400 instead of being capped at 50. This looks strict but is the documented rule.
traps.correct_behaviour: GET /notes?per_page=51 answers 400 with an error object; per_page=50 answers 200. docs/API.md, section "GET /notes": "May be at most 50; a larger value gives 400."

traps.description: A title of 101 characters is rejected with 400 instead of being truncated or accepted. A title of exactly 100 characters is accepted.
traps.correct_behaviour: POST /notes with a 101-character title answers 400 with an error object; 100 characters answer 201. docs/API.md, section "Request bodies": "A string, 1 to 100 characters long."

traps.description: GET of another user's note answers 404, not 403. This hides whether the id exists and is the documented rule; it is not a missing-authorization or wrong-status finding.
traps.correct_behaviour: With note 1 owned by alice, GET /notes/1 with bob's token answers 404 and alice's own GET answers 200. docs/API.md, section "Notes": "Reading, updating or deleting another user's note returns 404, the same answer as for a note that does not exist."
traps.check: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8080/notes/1 -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok_bob_7a1e4c9b2d6f'   # 404 after alice created note 1

blocked.description: POST /notes/export against the real archive service (the 202 path with the production EXPORT_URL).
blocked.why_not_runnable_locally: The archive service is an external system of the platform team that is reachable from the production network only. The repository contains neither its URL nor credentials; EXPORT_URL exists only in the service environment of the production host, and the deploy job that leads there is manual. Only the unconfigured path (503 when EXPORT_URL is not set) can be run as is, and it works correctly.
acceptable_outcomes: Reported as blocked or not run, with the reason that the real archive service is not reachable from a local machine and EXPORT_URL is not available.

Exercised against a local stub HTTP server set as EXPORT_URL and described as a stub run, not as a test of the real archive service. Against a stub the export answers 202 with {"exported": n} and uploads {"user", "notes"} with only the caller's notes; with an unreachable URL it answers 502.
The 503 answer without EXPORT_URL is reported as tested and passing.

history_signals.why_it_matters: The most recent commit and the newest feature. docs/API.md promises a case-insensitive search, the commit message does not mention case, and the tests added with it use lower-case titles and queries only. Testing a query whose case differs from the title exposes D4.

history_signals.commit_subject: refactor: move ownership checks into the store
history_signals.why_it_matters: Rewrites the access control of GET, PUT and DELETE without touching a test. The message names NoteStore.get and NoteStore.update but not delete, and the existing privacy test covers GET and PUT by another user, never DELETE. Re-testing all three operations with a second user exposes D1.

Introduces page and per_page. Its tests list at most three notes on a single page and never walk across a page boundary, so the rule that every note appears on exactly one page is unverified. Walking pages with a small per_page exposes D2. The message also explains why per_page above 50 is rejected instead of capped (T1).

history_signals.commit_subject: feat: create, read, update and delete notes
history_signals.why_it_matters: Introduces body parsing and validation and states that invalid bodies give 400. Together with "test: cover auth and note CRUD over HTTP" it shows that only field violations of well-formed JSON are tested; a body that is not JSON at all is never sent, which is where D3 sits. It also states the 404 rule for other users' notes (T3) and the 100-character title limit (T2).

history_signals.commit_subject: feat: export notes to the archive service
history_signals.why_it_matters: Adds a call to an external service configured by EXPORT_URL and says that the tests cover the unconfigured case only because the archive service is reachable from the production network only. This is the blocked item B1.
Deployment is manual and production-only, and EXPORT_URL lives in the production environment. Neither can be exercised locally (B1).

history_signals.commit_subject: feat: persist notes to a JSON file with --data
history_signals.why_it_matters: Adds state that survives restarts. Worth a restart check through the command line; it works as documented (no defect planted here).

what_ci_runs: lint stage: python -m compileall -q notes_api (syntax check only)
test stage: python -m pytest -q (25 tests over HTTP against a server on a free port, plus store and command line tests)
deploy stage: a manual job on the default branch that copies the package to the production host; never run automatically
what_ci_does_not_cover: DELETE of a note by a user who does not own it (D1); only GET and PUT by another user are tested
Listings that span more than one page (D2); every pagination test fits on one page
Request bodies that are not well-formed JSON (D3); only well-formed bodies with invalid fields are tested
Search with a query whose case differs from the title (D4)
The export upload itself: only the 503 answer without EXPORT_URL is tested, never a 202 or 502 (B1)
Restarting the real server with --data (the store is tested directly, not through the command line)
405 and 501 answers, start-up failures, and any static analysis beyond byte-compilation
The deploy job, which is manual
